page: Amazon Web Services d2.8xlarge is a dense storage instance in the Storage Optimized family, built on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor running at 2.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 36 vCPUs across 18 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation. It includes 244.0 GB of memory (6.78 GB per core), 30 MB of L3 cache, and lacks dedicated GPUs. A defining hardware feature is its bundled local storage array comprising 49,152 GB of HDD capacity, accompanied by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance trade-offs inherent to the older processor architecture. Single-core performance is limited, with Geekbench single-core (902.0) and stress-ng single-core (740.99) placing in the bottom 10%, alongside weak single-threaded compression throughput. However, its 36 vCPUs allow it to achieve solid mid-range multi-core efficiency, reaching a PassMark CPU score of 28,310.78, Geekbench multi-core score of 7,844.0, and balanced multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 55.59 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains in the middle 50% category, measuring 89.34 GB/sec for large read operations and 36.67 GB/sec for writes.

From an infrastructure perspective, the d2.8xlarge offers exceptional local HDD storage density per compute unit, making it cost-efficient for storage-intensive processing relative to provisioning detached network volumes. Because of modest single-core throughput and older instruction set support (lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions), it is ill-suited for intensive machine learning text generation or low-latency transactional workloads. Instead, it is well matched for distributed file systems, massive batch processing, data warehousing, MapReduce jobs, and Hadoop clusters requiring high local capacity and reliable sequential throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services d2.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.4 GHz. It features 36 dedicated vCPUs across 18 physical cores, 244.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled local storage capacity of 49,152 GB on HDDs, with a 10 Gbps baseline network link. While single-thread benchmarks place in the lower performance tiers (Geekbench single-core at 902.0), the 36-thread configuration delivers solid mid-range multi-core compute, posting a PassMark CPU score of 28,310.78 and 18.54 GB/sec static web throughput. With significant storage density paired with substantial system memory, the instance delivers strong density efficiency for sequential data pipelines, distributed file storage, MapReduce clusters, and large-scale data warehousing workloads.
